Noah: Heads up - Pivot POC reporting repeated slow first-token latency after a 90s stress run. They see p50 jump from ~170ms to 700-1.2s intermittently.
Priya: are they on hosted or dedicated infra? any custom tuning?
Noah: hosted trial org. They enabled prefill per our quickstart and used a tight batch window.
Helena: diag-bot, what runtime and recent deploys in region?
diag-bot: runtime `v2.13.2` deployed to `us-west-2` at 07:58 PT. No infra alerts.
Sam: what's the prefill config and client concurrency? small batch windows + concurrency often cause KV cache thrash.
Noah: customer pasted config: `prefill: enabled, prefill_batch_window_ms: 200, max_prefill_tokens: 400`, concurrency ~14, model `redwood-2-8b-quant`, avg prompt 110 tokens.
Rosa: did they see rate-limits or 429s around the time?
Noah: yes, a short spike of 429s during the stress run then later TTFT spikes.
Priya: ask them for the session diag: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/diag/session/<sid>?fields=queue,kvcache,rate` and paste key lines.
Noah: they returned: `queue_wait_ms=380, kvcache_miss=true, backend_ms=84, x-ratelimit-remaining=72`.
Helena: kvcache_miss=true with high queue_wait is a classic sign of write/read races across shards from many small prefill batches.
Sam: mitigation steps: 1) Temporarily disable prefill to verify baseline; 2) Increase `prefill_batch_window_ms` to 800-1200ms to batch prefill writes; 3) Turn on `prefill_strict_sequencing` to serialize writes per session (slower prefill but stable reads).
Rosa: customer concerned about demo SLA (they need p50 < 300ms). Also asking if we can credit POC days affected.
Priya: recommend quick test: A) disable prefill and rerun the same load pattern for 3-5 mins; B) if p50 recovers, propose controlled re-enable with larger batch window while we monitor.
Noah: customer disabled prefill and reported p50 ~ 230ms, no 429s during a 6-min replay.
Helena: that confirms prefill interaction. For re-enable, suggest API patch snippet in the email: `PATCH /v1/projects/<proj>/settings { "prefill": { "enabled": true, "prefill_batch_window_ms": 1000, "prefill_strict_sequencing": false } }`.
Sam: also include diag command in the email so they can share any future snaps quickly. And ask them to include `x-ratelimit-*` headers when they see errors.
Priya: ops note - if re-enable shows instability we can flip to `prefill_strict_sequencing: true` as fallback and run a quick impact test.
Rosa: for the credit ask, I'll draft a conditional goodwill credit: one day of hosted usage if instability remains after our guided re-enable and monitoring window. Sales ops to approve.
diag-bot: ticket #7129 updated: "Performed temp prefill disable; p50 improved to ~230ms. Plan: controlled re-enable with larger batch window TOM 09:00 PT; team monitoring."
Noah: customer agreed to 09:00 PT controlled re-enable and invited Lina from their infra team.
Helena: I'll bring per-shard queue tail script and KV hit-rate dashboard; Sam will have rollback runbook ready.
Sam: follow-ups: ["monitor kvcache hit-rate during re-enable","capture per-shard queue_wait_ms","verify no 429s and check x-ratelimit headers","prepare quick rollback to disable prefill"]
Priya: thanks team. Noah, please paste the email template into the POC ticket and link the repro commands.
Noah: done, closing loop after the re-enable with a short postmortem and metric snapshot. :thumbsup:
followUps: verify no 429s and check x-ratelimit headers
prepare quick rollback to disable prefill
